text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Finnish high school students take part in pan-European "Journalist for a Day" event by making up pages of Helsingin Sanomat in plexiglass office at the the main railway station.
- A satellite guidance system developed by the U.S. military for its cruise missiles now helps Finnish logging trucks navigate.
- Growing ranks of unemployed youth raise concerns over the emergence of a new underclass.
- Conservative Party begins its local government election campaign in earnest with party leader Sauli Niinisto setting job creation as its main campaign theme.
- Head of Finnish UFO watchers' organisation says corn circles found in an Espoo field are a hoax.
- Economics Professor Jukka Pekkarinen writes in a signed column that Parliament should set goals for monetary policy, including target inflation rate.
KAUPPALEHTI

- Finnish Broadcasting Company YLE television chief Heikki Lehmusto says YLE will hold its own despite increased competition from new commercial TV channel. But Lehmusto says a price war would be dangerous for the industry.
- Bond issue profits and interest revenues enhance State budget by two billion markka this year.
- Companies testing a more flexible approach to budgeting.
DEMARI
- 1997 tax cut will add 400 markka to pay packets of workers now earning 10,000 markka per month. Unions call it a "historical boost in purchasing power".
AAMULEHTI

- Finance ministry official says 45-50 billion markka in subsidies paid to bail banks out of the crisis of the 1990s will never be recovered. By end-July, subsidies had also cost 11.1 billion markka in interest.
- Many drunk drivers think they have already sobered up from previous night's drinking when they get behind the wheel.
- Speaker of Parliament Riitta Uosukainen draws audience of 1,000 at a church in northwest Finland after publishing her sensationally frank memoirs.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Sunday evening fire at a Turku city hospital darkened operating rooms.

- Opposition Centre Party leader Esko Aho said Finland should allow markka to continue to float and that ERM is not a prerequisite for joining EMU, as long as currency is stable for the required two years.
- Finnish team comes third in international German Shepherd dog skills contest.
